texte.L’article #, §#, b), exige des délais de: Article #(#)(b) requires notice periods and notification obligations in the contract. That is where your own clock is negotiated.
texte.L’article #, §#, exige de tenir compte d: Article #(#) requires taking into account the vulnerabilities SPECIFIC to each direct supplier, not a generic supplier policy.
texte.L’article #, §#, impose une SECONDE noti: Article #(#) imposes a SECOND notification, to the recipients of the services, separate from the one to the CSIRT. And paragraph # requires you to tell them what they can apply themselves.

texte.L’article #er, §#, ne vise que les entit: Article #(#) targets only FINANCIAL entities, which Article #(#) limits to points (a) to (t). A hosting provider serving banks remains fully under NIS #: it is the costliest misreading on the market.

texte.L’empreinte croise trois postes jamais c: The footprint cross-checks three items that are never confused: use (electricity × the country’s carbon intensity, # edition, life cycle), the manufacturing of equipment amortised over its lifetime, and cooling water. On a highly decarbonised grid, manufacturing weighs more than use — a reading that showed only use would wrongly rank Sweden close to zero.

texte.L’indice ne vaut que par la fraîcheur de: The index is only as good as the freshness of what feeds it: a high score calculated on assessments from a year ago proves nothing. Date your campaigns and redo them at least annually.

texte.L’onglet « Enveloppe & DPGF » transforme: The “Envelope & DPGF” tab turns the ranking into a decision: power, template, scenario — new build, extension or takeover — and up to six countries compared. It gives the envelope as a range, its BREAKDOWN INTO FOURTEEN LOTS, annual operation, total cost and a phased schedule up to #. Two things must be known before using it. First, it DOES NOT MAKE YOUR PRICE. The cost per megawatt comes from a published survey — Soben, part of Accenture, Data Centre Trends Report #: from $# to $# million per MW for cloud, up to $# million for a gigawatt-scale AI campus — converted from dollars at a displayed rate, because a daily rate is not framework data. This source covers cloud and AI campuses, NOT colocation or the regional site, whose nature remains marked accordingly. And it remains a market order of magnitude: since none of the # sites in the framework publishes its capacity, nothing here replaces your quotes. A new lever is added, the SCHEDULE: the same source puts at +# % the premium a hyperscaler accepted to meet a tight deadline, and the module translates it into euros — the premium buys the priority of a general contractor, never the grid operator’s agreement, and the connection lead time therefore remains a floor. Second, for the same power the envelope is IDENTICAL from one country to another, for lack of a national cost index in this framework: what separates them is read in the total cost, where the price of electricity multiplied by the PUE and carbon open gaps of more than a quarter over ten years. Five items — land, labour, share of connection costs, taxation, contractual electricity price — are shown EMPTY, with the question to ask: they can reverse the ranking on their own, and hiding them would give the illusion of a complete decision. The result also carries its MAP: the two to six countries compared are coloured from best to least good, each with its rank — and the rank is that of the TOTAL COST, never of the investment, since that is identical by construction and would give a uniform fill. The other countries remain grey, and the legend says what that grey means: they have not lost, they have not been calculated.
texte.L’onglet « Prospectives #-# » répond à l: The “Outlook #-#” tab answers the limitation of the rest of the page: a framework is a SNAPSHOT, whereas an investment decision is made over five to ten years. It carries the dated facts of four reports from named publishers — Soben part of Accenture for the # trends, three Accenture studies for energy, sustainable AI and non-financial reporting. Each entry gives its PAGE and, in nineteen cases out of twenty-five, its VERBATIM QUOTATION; the other six summarise an entire section and say so, rather than suggesting a word-for-word quote. When a report only REPEATS a figure, the real author is named alongside: the edge market forecast is by Research and Markets, not Soben. First read the first block, the CAVEATS: they are the only entries that call into question a figure displayed elsewhere on this page. The Finnish price class, for example, rests on a # Eurostat series — prior to the removal of the reduced excise rate in March #, which adds about €#/MWh. The class is NOT recalculated, for lack of a series published since, and that is deliberate: a framework that rewrites itself without saying so loses track of what was cited the week before. The caveat is dated, placed next to the value, and carried over as it is into the envelope file of the country concerned. Next come ten regulatory milestones sorted by date — a freeze on AI projects in Frankfurt until #, no new projects in Amsterdam before #, mandatory waste heat recovery in Germany from # July #, a European energy efficiency package expected in the first quarter of # — then the ten trends, each saying WHICH comparator criterion it affects, or that it affects none: that last mention is information, the framework does not capture everything. These lists are read BY DIPPING IN, never straight through: each entry is an expandable panel, and they are arranged TWO PER ROW. Collapsed, a panel is never mute — it carries what lets you decide whether to open it: the country and the criterion targeted for a caveat, the date and status for a milestone, the comparator criterion for a trend, the value and its nature for a market fact. The same treatment applies to the “Sources, method and verification” section — texts applied, public data sources, acknowledged limits — and to the REGISTER OF FACT CHECKS, where the verdict remains visible without opening: a register that forced you to expand everything to find its unfavourable verdicts would not be verifiable, it would be promotional. Only the constants table remains a table: it is a comparison grid, and collapsing it row by row would prevent precisely the comparison.
